title: Partition Array into Two Equal Product Subsets
summary: Given an integer array nums containing distinct positive integers and an integer target, determine if it is possible to partition nums into two non-empty disjoint subsets such that the product of the elements in each subset equals the target.
statement: Given an integer array nums containing distinct positive integers and an integer target, determine if it is possible to partition nums into two non-empty disjoint subsets such that the product of the elements in each subset equals the target. Return true if such a partition exists, and false otherwise. A subset of an array is a selection of elements from the array.
constraints: nums has 3 to 12 distinct positive integers, each at most 100.
Partition every element into two nonempty subsets.
Both subset products must equal target, which may be as large as 10^15.
hints: If both subset products equal target, the product of the entire array must be target squared.
After the necessary total-product check, enumerate proper nonempty subset masks and test one side’s product.
Reject total!=target²; multiply selected elements for masks 1 through 2^n-2 and accept a product equal to target.
The complement is nonempty by the mask bounds and automatically has product target because the total is target².
editorial: The complement is nonempty by the mask bounds and automatically has product target because the total is target².

tests.explanation: No partition makes both subset products equal 15.
